source.title: Stochastic Gradient Descent With Hyperbolic-Tangent Decay on Classification
source.authors: Bo-Yang Hsueh; Wei Li; I-Chen Wu

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports scheduler comparisons on natural-label classification, but it does not test the claim’s random-label memorization/generalization coexistence, width beyond interpolation, architecture bias, optimizer generalization, batch-size effects, dropout effects, generalization-gap measures, or memorized-example removal.
record.gate_note: The scheduler results on CIFAR, ImageNet, Fashion-MNIST and PAMAP2 compare HTD with step and cosine schedules; none measures training error versus test error, random-label fitting, or a versioned claim condition. Values mentioned about cited prior work are not this paper’s results.
record.test_reason: The study compares learning-rate schedules within Nesterov SGD. It discusses adaptive methods' generalization and switching from Adam to SGD, but reports no adaptive-optimizer comparison. Its own experiments do not test any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: they claim HTD outperforms step decay in all experiments and cosine in nearly all cases, recommend HTD(-6,3) as a default, and acknowledge that optimal parameters vary by dataset and setting. This describes their overall conclusion; individual HTD configurations do not uniformly outperform every comparator.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies learning-rate scheduling performance on classification benchmarks, not the claim’s generalization-gap or memorization methods.
record.method_sensitivity: HTD performance changes with L, U and their ratio; the best ratio differs by dataset, epoch count and settings.

fits_no_version.finding: HTD scheduling generally lowers held-out error relative to step decay and cosine scheduling. Performance depends on schedule parameters, dataset, and training duration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate schedule choice within Nesterov SGD affects held-out classification performance.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Workshop/Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
record.problems: The paper reports test error rates and run counts, but does not report training errors or directly measure a training–test gap. Several ImageNet comparisons reuse cited results; some runs are limited (ResNet-34 HTD has one run).
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the reported scheduler comparison results do not bear on any listed claim version.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Widening beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers.
Large versus small batches under matched epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a batch-size penalty.
Dropout effects and its interaction with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Keep the empty version-linked row set. Different batch sizes across architectures do not constitute a controlled batch-size test. The absence of training-error measurements is not itself decisive: the missing version-specific comparisons are what prevent these scheduler results from testing the claims.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error and resulting test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance under tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch effects on the training–test gap.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Effect of removing memorized examples on test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
